title: Chocolate-Topped Butter Toffee
summary: Crisp, nut-free butter toffee cooked to 149 °C, topped with melted dark chocolate and cut into rectangles.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, cubed, plus a little for the tin
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Line the tin with baking paper, leaving an overhang, and butter the paper lightly.

steps.title: Melt it together
steps.text: Put the butter, sugar, corn syrup, water and salt in the saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the butter has melted and the sugar has dissolved.

steps.title: Cook to 149 °C
steps.text: Keep cooking, stirring slowly but steadily, for 15-20 min. It will foam, then thicken and darken. Stop when it reads 149 °C and is the colour of peanut butter.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vanilla; it will spit, so stand back. Pour straight into the tin and tilt it so the toffee spreads evenly.

steps.title: Add the chocolate
steps.text: Wait 2 min, then scatter the chocolate over the hot toffee. Leave it for 3 min until it looks glossy and soft, then spread it to the edges with the offset spatula.

steps.title: Let it set
steps.text: Leave at room temperature for 1 h, then chill for 30 min until the chocolate is firm.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Lift the slab out and cut it into 32 rectangles, pressing the knife straight down rather than sawing.

tips: The most common mistake is stopping below 149 °C; underdone toffee is chewy and sticks to your teeth instead of snapping.
If butter separates out as an oily layer, take the pan off the heat and stir hard for a minute, then carry on.
Let the toffee come back to room temperature for 10 min before cutting so the chocolate does not crack.
Hot toffee causes severe burns; keep children away.
storage: Keep in an airtight container, layered with baking paper, at cool room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
